messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: multiple GPU nodes (cluster: inference-prod-us-west) reporting repeated OOMs and container restarts on paged-attn workers. Grouping by node shows slow memory creep across KV cache shards. Auto-retries increasing, tail latency spiking. Pager: miranda.

miranda: seeing it, joining. logs look noisy. OOM kworker traces + CUDA driver resets.

sam: :eyes: I pulled the last 10m logs -> lots of 'cudaMemcpyAsync failed' then container crash. stack shows kv allocator hitting vmem high-water.

jin: node-level metrics: DRAM usage trending up over 6 hours, allocator fragmentation slowly increasing. Paging metrics show many small free fragments. possible KV slab leak on long-lived sessions.

rohan: customer-impact?

customer-support: a few customers reported timeouts for text-gen endpoints ~2-3% of requests in the last 30m, mainly long-context chats. No widespread 5xx reports yet but retries visible.

miranda: mitigation plan: 1) reduce long-context routing -> force short-context model variant to relieve KV pressure 2) enable immediate slab eviction flag on affected node pool 3) scale out with spare capacity and enable fallback routing. Doing (1) now.

sam: how do we toggle short-context routing?

miranda: updating routing policy in console -> set route inference.chat.long_context.enabled = false for prod-us-west. applying.

deploy-bot: Route update submitted: change-set 1765. Applying to prod-us-west.

miranda: applied. starting a small canary reroute for 10% of traffic.

sam: running quick GC/defrag on KV cache on node gpu-17, command:
```
# run on node
grpcctl kvcache defrag --pool paged-attn --level aggressive --drain 30s
```
Output: started defrag job, will fragment-merge asynchronously.

jin: defrag kicked off on gpu-17 -> memory dip ~2%. But other nodes still creeping. Need broader action.

rohan: can we cordon/restart affected pods to force cold start and release fragments?

sam: we can, but cold starts may cause transient latency. Recommend draining one node at a time from the pool and letting warmup run on a spare.

miranda: proceeding with planned rolling drain of 2 nodes. will monitor tail-latency.

(10m later)

miranda: drain done for gpu-17 and gpu-22. both restarted, memory baseline lower. saw a handful of elevated latencies during warmup but no errors.

jin: but gpu-19 still shows slow memory climb; fragmentation ratio high. I want to flip the 'evict-on-fragment-threshold' lower while we dig into allocator behavior.

sam: lowering config:```
# infra config
allocator.paged_attn.evict_fragment_threshold = 0.65
allocator.paged_attn.background_compact = true
```
applied to pool.

rohan: what's the risk? more evictions could hurt throughput and push more CPU. agree keep watch.

miranda: agreed. watch CPU/RPS.

(20m later)

sam: cuda driver logs show repeated "NVRM: GPU at PCI:0000:65:00: GPU has fallen off the bus" around crashes. Those match container restarts. Could be memory overcommit at driver level exposing fragmentation.

jin: nvml output shows process retention on GPU even after container exit sometimes. Force nvidia-smi -r was used earlier but not always effective.

miranda: notes for next step: schedule controlled restarts of driver on nodes with sticky GPU state. Doing one node restart at a time.

deploy-bot: Reminder: driver restarts may require infra approval for prod. Confirming rollback windows.

miranda: approved by rohan for emergency. initiating restart on gpu-19.

(commands)
```
sudo systemctl stop nvidia-persistenced
sudo rmmod nvidia_uvm nvidia
modprobe nvidia
systemctl start nvidia-persistenced
```

sam: driver restart completed on gpu-19. memory counters reset. container restarts stopped for that node.

jin: good signal. aggregate memory usage across pool dropped ~8%.

miranda: customer-impact trending down. still seeing a couple of degraded requests that hit long context before routing flip.

customer-support: customers on older SDKs may still hit long-context routes for a short window; sending advisory to affected accounts.

rohan: action items for root cause: 1) snapshot allocator metrics for last 48h 2) instrument KV cache for per-shard leak detection 3) add an emergency compaction path that can be triggered via console 4) do postmortem if leak confirmed.

sam: I can submit a hotfix that adds a periodic compaction job targeting small-fragment buckets. will prototype on staging.

miranda: handoff time in 38m. who will take follow-ups?

sam: I'll stay on until compaction prototype deployed to canary.

jin: I'll collect dmesg, nvml dumps and heap profiles for the nodes we drained.

rohan: I'll coordinate customer comms and track SLO impact.

miranda: okay drafting handoff: SUMMARY: slow KV cache fragmentation + driver instability caused progressive OOMs and container restarts on paged-attn pool. Mitigations done: short-context routing flip, rolling drains + defrag, lowered evict threshold, targeted driver restart on sticky nodes, scale-out fallback routing. Current state: traffic rerouted for long-context; pool stabilized; occasional elevated tail latency during warmups. Customer impact: small % of requests timed out (~2-3%) during peak, no major data loss. Next steps: compaction hotfix PR, better per-shard metrics/alerts, enable emergency-compaction button in console, run load test with long-context retention to reproduce.

miranda: handoff to sam (on-call) at 4150003600. I'll ping infra and release a post-incident page. :white_check_mark:

sam: ack. I'll keep the canary on for 2 hours and post updates to this thread.

rohan: thumbs for my part. preparing brief to send to support and AMs.

(reacts)
miranda: :thumbsup: sam: :eyes: jin: :mag:

incident-bot: incident closed for active-alerts after stabilization window. If metrics regress, re-open or escalate to Eng Runtime.

sam: adding final note: avoid full pool restarts next time; prefer incremental drains + defrag + targeted driver restarts. logging follow-ups in infra ticket INF-1287.
